numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Comparing a TimeDelta with a NaN Quantity (e.g. TimeDelta(5, format="sec") < (np.nan * u.s)) raises TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'TimeDelta' and 'Quantity' instead of returning False.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The comparison should return False, similar to comparisons with np.nan (e.g. TimeDelta(1, format="sec") < np.nan * u.s should evaluate to False; likewise <= and > should be False).
trigger_conditions: Left operand is a TimeDelta object
Right operand is a Quantity holding a nan value with a time unit (e.g. np.nan * u.s or u.Quantity(np.nan, unit=u.s))

category_specific_evidence: Special value involved is NaN, in the right-hand operand: a Quantity holding np.nan in seconds, e.g. TimeDelta(5, format="sec") < (np.nan * u.s), raised TypeError instead of returning False (issue #15230).
Expected handling per the issue text: comparing with NaN should return False, similar to other comparisons with np.nan.

Regression test test_time_delta_comp_nan_quantity uses dt1 = TimeDelta(1, format="sec") and dt2 = np.nan * u.s, and asserts not dt1 < dt2, not dt2 > dt1, not dt1 <= dt2, not dt2 >= dt1, not dt1 > dt2, not dt2 < dt1, not dt1 >= dt2, not dt2 <= dt1, dt1 != dt2 (True), and not dt1 == dt2.
Companion test test_time_delta_comp_num_quantity checks the same ordering with the finite quantity 2 * u.s and expects dt1 < dt2 to be True.

Finiteness check in astropy/time/formats.py: the renamed _check_finite_vals (formerly _check_val_type) requires val1 to be finite (no NaN or inf), while val2 may contain NaN. A class attribute _check_finite = True is added to TimeFormat and is meant to be overridden to False in subclasses where NaN and inf are valid inputs.
The fix is PR #15830, described as fixing comparison of a NaN quantity with a TimeDelta object; the regression test was added for bug 15230.
